articles.title: A technical SEO audit starts with crawlability, indexability, and intent
articles.metaDescription: A practical way to review technical SEO evidence, prioritize blockers, and turn findings into verifiable actions.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: A measured audit begins with evidence: whether important pages can be discovered, crawled, indexed, and understood.

blocks.text: A technical SEO audit is most useful when it answers a business question, not when it produces the longest spreadsheet. Start with the pages that matter, collect evidence, and separate confirmed problems from assumptions.
Start with the page and the evidence

Choose a representative set of important pages: a category, a product or service page, an editorial page, and the main conversion page. Record each page's response status, canonical, robots directives, title, internal links, and available Search Console or crawl evidence. Note the source and date of each observation.

items: Can users and crawlers reach the page?
Does the page have a consistent canonical and indexability directive?
Does its visible content match the intended search need?
Can a user reach it through relevant internal links?
Which claim is supported by data, and which still needs verification?

blocks.text: Prioritize blockers before polish

A useful order is access and response problems, indexability and canonical conflicts, important content gaps, internal discovery, then refinements. The order can change with the site and business goal; state why a task is urgent rather than assigning a made-up traffic impact.
Make each finding actionable

Write findings as evidence, likely consequence, confidence, and next verification step. For example: “The supplied crawl export reports a noindex directive on the category page; confirm the live response and whether exclusion is intentional before changing it.” This is clearer and safer than saying the page has been removed from search based on one file.

blocks.title: A note on tools
blocks.text: A checklist or AI prompt can organize supplied evidence; it does not replace a live crawl, Search Console access, or an experienced reviewer. Never upload credentials or private customer data to a public model.
A concise handoff

For each task, name the affected URL pattern, the evidence, the person who can verify it, and the acceptance check. Keep unresolved questions visible. This makes an audit a working plan rather than a static report.

articles.title: Meta Ads objectives: align campaign setup with business outcomes
articles.metaDescription: A planning checklist for choosing a Meta Ads campaign objective, defining a useful conversion, and validating the measurement plan.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: Plan from the business outcome and conversion signal, then validate current campaign settings and policy in Meta's official resources.
articles.disclaimer: Advertising interfaces, objectives, policies, and available measurement options change. Verify current details in the official platform before campaign launch.

blocks.text: A campaign objective is a setup choice, not a business strategy by itself. Before selecting one, define what the business needs to learn or achieve and how that outcome will be measured.
Write down the outcome first

Describe the desired action in plain language: a qualified enquiry, a completed purchase, or a useful visit to a product page. Then check whether the website or lead process records that action reliably. If measurement is incomplete, call that out before treating campaign results as conclusive.

items: Who is the intended audience, and which exclusions are necessary?
What exact action should the campaign encourage?
Where does that action happen, and is tracking configured with consent?
Which offer claims are approved and supportable?
What is the smallest meaningful creative test?

blocks.text: Match the objective to the measurement

Review Meta's current objective options and choose the one that best corresponds to the campaign outcome and available conversion signal. The interface and objective names may change. Do not select an objective simply because a platform recommends it without checking whether the optimization event reflects the real business goal.
Test a clear hypothesis

Change one meaningful creative or message variable at a time where practical. Define the audience, landing page, observation period, and decision rule before launch. Avoid promising a result from a small or noisy sample.

blocks.title: Policy and privacy check
blocks.text: Check current Meta advertising policies, regional requirements, consent, and any restrictions relevant to the product or audience. Do not target or exclude people using sensitive personal attributes.
Keep a reviewable campaign brief

Record the objective, audience rationale, approved claims, conversion event, creative hypothesis, budget assumptions, and policy review date. A brief makes later learning easier and gives a reviewer a clear way to catch mismatches before launch.

articles.title: Google Ads keyword research: turn intent into an account structure
articles.metaDescription: Use verified keyword data and landing-page intent to build a reviewable Google Ads structure without guessing demand or cost.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: A practical sequence for researching search terms, grouping intent, and matching keywords to landing pages.
articles.disclaimer: Google Ads features, keyword metrics, and campaign controls can change. Verify current details and forecasts in the official account and documentation.

blocks.text: A useful paid-search structure connects what a person searches for to a relevant ad and landing page. Keyword lists are inputs to that decision, not a substitute for understanding intent or checking the account's actual data.
Begin with the offer and the searcher

Write down the product, service area, language, audience, and conversion goal. Expand from genuine customer questions and product terminology, then use an authorized source such as Keyword Planner to research terms and available estimates.

items: Keep the source and date beside any metric.
Separate research ideas from terms approved for a campaign.
Group by meaning and landing-page fit rather than superficial wording.
Mark ambiguous or irrelevant terms for review.
Check whether the page fulfills the promise implied by the keyword and ad.

blocks.text: Build groups around coherent intent

A group should contain terms that can be served by a consistent message and destination. If terms imply different products, audiences, or stages of decision, splitting them may make the campaign easier to understand and report on. There is no universal number of keywords per group.
Treat forecasts as estimates

Keyword planning tools can show estimates based on their data and settings. They are not guarantees of traffic, cost, or results. Preserve assumptions about location, dates, match settings, and budget when discussing an estimate.

blocks.title: Before import
blocks.text: Review match settings, negative terms, ad policy, conversion measurement, and landing-page relevance in the current Google Ads interface. Do not bulk-upload an automatically generated structure without a person checking it.

articles.title: LinkedIn Ads targeting: focus the audience before scaling
articles.metaDescription: A B2B campaign planning checklist for translating a business audience into a focused LinkedIn Ads test and a measurable lead path.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: Translate a clearly described B2B audience into a focused test, then validate current targeting and lead-form settings in LinkedIn's official documentation.
articles.disclaimer: LinkedIn campaign controls and policies can change. Verify targeting options, privacy requirements, and product availability in the current official documentation.

blocks.text: B2B targeting is easier to evaluate when the audience is defined by a real business need rather than a long list of filters. Start with the role in the buying process, the type of organization, and the problem the campaign addresses.
Describe the audience before opening the campaign builder

items: Which organizations have a genuine need for the offer?
Which job functions or seniority levels are relevant to the decision?
Which locations and languages are in scope?
What exclusions prevent wasted or inappropriate delivery?
What audience size or delivery constraints need review in the platform?

blocks.text: Use job titles and professional attributes only when they help identify the business audience. A highly specific audience can make a campaign difficult to deliver or interpret; a very broad one may make the message less relevant. Treat the first setup as a hypothesis to test.
Connect the message to a useful next step

Match the ad's promise to the landing page or lead form. Explain what happens after a person submits details, collect only what is needed, and confirm the privacy notice and consent language are appropriate for the market.
Measure lead quality, not just form volume

Agree on how a qualified lead is defined and how it will be reviewed by the sales team. Where permitted, connect campaign reporting to downstream outcomes. Do not claim that a lower-cost form submission is valuable until the business checks its quality.

blocks.title: Before scaling
blocks.text: Check LinkedIn's current audience, Lead Gen Form, consent, and advertising policies. Confirm that the tracking path is lawful, configured, and actually records the intended outcome.

articles.title: Evaluate AI tools with a repeatable test, not a first impression
articles.metaDescription: A practical evaluation framework for comparing AI tools using a defined task, representative examples, source checks, and clear limitations.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: Define the task and evaluation criteria first, then compare representative outputs and check sources, privacy, and human-review needs.
articles.disclaimer: AI products, models, capabilities, and terms change. This guide describes a testing method, not a current product ranking.

blocks.text: A new AI product can feel impressive in a short demo, but that does not establish whether it is useful for your work. A small, repeatable evaluation is more informative: use a real task, representative inputs, and criteria decided before comparing outputs.
Write down the task and constraints

Describe the job in terms of its input, expected output, acceptable errors, time constraints, and review requirements. Use sanitized examples that resemble the actual work without exposing client data or credentials.
Create a small evaluation set

items: Include ordinary inputs and a few realistic edge cases.
Define what a good answer must contain and what would make it unacceptable.
Run the same inputs through each candidate and record model/version and date.
Check factual claims against authoritative sources.
Record latency, workflow fit, and editing effort only if you actually measured them.

blocks.text: Review privacy and operational fit

Before testing with real material, check data retention, access controls, terms, regional requirements, integrations, and how the output will be reviewed. Prefer fictional or redacted examples during early evaluation.

blocks.title: No universal winner
blocks.text: Results depend on the task, prompt, model version, configuration, and evaluation set. Do not turn a small test into a broad claim about which tool is best.
Make the decision auditable

Keep a brief record of the criteria, sample inputs, observed differences, limitations, and decision owner. Re-test when the model, product terms, or workflow changes. A lightweight record might look like this:

articles.title: Review an n8n workflow before you run it
articles.metaDescription: A safety-first checklist for inspecting workflow triggers, network requests, credentials, data handling, and side effects before activation.
articles.author: Ayoub Yatouji
articles.summary: Inspect every workflow trigger and node, follow the path of credentials and data, then test with fictional inputs before enabling it.
articles.disclaimer: This checklist is general guidance, not a security certification. n8n documentation and version-specific controls may change.

blocks.text: A workflow export is executable configuration, not just a diagram. Before importing or activating one, understand what starts it, which nodes run, where data goes, and what changes the workflow can make.
Inspect the full execution path

items: Identify manual, schedule, webhook, and event triggers.
Review every HTTP request and the destination it contacts.
Check file, shell, database, and write operations for their side effects.
Trace which fields are passed to each external service.
Confirm that credentials are referenced through the platform's credential manager, not embedded in exported JSON.

blocks.text: Test with minimal, fictional data

Keep the workflow inactive while reviewing it. Run a small manual test with fictional values, inspect the output, and check error paths. Only then consider connecting authorized credentials with the narrowest appropriate permissions.
Plan ownership and failure handling
Decide who owns the workflow, how failures are noticed, how long execution data is retained, and how to disable the automation. Document external services and any user or customer data processed.

blocks.title: Never execute blindly
blocks.text: Do not run a downloaded workflow because its title or publisher looks familiar. Inspect its nodes, destinations, permissions, and version first.
A useful starter is deliberately limited

The demonstration workflows in this hub use manual triggers and Set nodes only. They do not call APIs, access a file system, or include credentials. Treat them as learning examples, not production-ready automations.
